title: "Brain-Controlled Robot for Assisting Basic Upper Limb Tasks"

---

This project explores **EEG-based control of a robotic arm** to assist individuals with upper-limb motor impairments.  
By translating brain activity into robotic commands, the system enables users to perform essential actions—such as **grasping, releasing, or resting**—through thought-triggered muscle movements (e.g., blinking or jaw clenching).

---

### 🧠 Overview
- **Conference Demo:** IEEE Body Sensor Networks (BSN) 2023  
- **Collaborators:** Dr. Mohammad Arif Ul Alam (UMass Lowell), Dr. João Luís G. Rosa (University of São Paulo)  
- **Hardware:** Muse 2 EEG headband, Raspberry Pi-based robotic arm  
- **Objective:** Restore limited upper-limb motion control via low-cost, portable EEG interface  

---

### ⚙️ System Design
The system converts raw EEG signals (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, theta) into control commands using a threshold-based event detector.  
The robot responds in real time to:
- **Blink events → Grasp**
- **Jaw clench events → Release**
- **Neutral state → No motion**

A Raspberry Pi processes classified EEG inputs and drives the robotic arm’s motors through serial communication.  

![](bci-setup.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

---

### 📊 Experimental Evaluation
Nine participants (ages 25–31) tested the prototype. A **6-question Likert survey** evaluated:
- Ease of use  
- Responsiveness  
- Comfort  
- Accuracy  

Results indicated **strong user satisfaction** and enthusiasm for extending the system to rehabilitation and assistive robotics.

### 💡 Impact & Future Work
This proof-of-concept demonstrates that **affordable EEG sensors** can power **real-time assistive robotics**.  
Next steps include:
- Expanding to **multi-channel EEG classification** for more complex gestures  
- Incorporating **machine learning** for adaptive signal mapping  
- Testing in **rehabilitation contexts** for neurodegenerative conditions
